editions: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the >>IMP reservation is §7.3.3 SR9 of the directive facility)
notes: Rule: A.1 item 30 'Compiler directives, compiler directive IMP (syntax rules and general rules). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for an IMP directive. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' (cite.py --check A.1 'compiler directive IMP (syntax rules and general rules)' -> OK §A.1 30). Clauses: §7.3.3 SR9 'If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the syntax rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined' -> OK §7.3.3 9); §7.3.4 GR4 '...the general rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined' -> OK §7.3.4 4). CONFORMANCE.md: no DOC-A.1-30 row (grep of '| DOC-A.1-30 |' empty; no mention of >>IMP anywhere in the doc). Code: no grammar or preprocessor rule recognizes IMP as a compiler-directive word (grep of src for an IMP directive finds only EC-*-IMP exception names). Probe /tmp/adj/probe/imp.cob ('>>IMP SOMETHING' before IDENTIFICATION DIVISION) -> 'error COBOL0001: unexpected '>'' rc=65: the directive is not defined, and it is refused as an anonymous parse error rather than named as an undefined implementor directive. The facility the item is conditioned on is ABSENT, so the obligation is not incurred; there is, however, no recorded posture ('Not provided.') for it, and PB280 Q1's 'Not provided.' -> DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT selector covers only OPTIONAL items, not conditionally required ones - extending it is an owner call (findings: conditional-facility-absent-posture). Owning notes: none specific (grep 'DOC-A.1-30\|item 30' hits only PB317's unrelated A.3 item 30); register umbrella A11 / PB160 (open).

editions: 2002, 2014, 2023 (national set from 2002; the alphanumeric half applies to every edition)
notes: Rule: A.1 item 31 'Computer's coded character set (characters in and encoding of computer's alphanumeric coded character set and computer's national coded character set, encoding for usage DISPLAY and usage NATIONAL). This item is required. This item shall be documented'. §8.1.2: 'The implementor shall specify the set of characters in and the encoding of each of the computer's alphanumeric character set and the computer's national character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-31 |' row. Fragments of an answer live in other items' rows: DOC-A.1-33/-188 ('Both native repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position'), DOC-A.1-209 ('One byte per character position' for USAGE DISPLAY), DOC-A.1-213 (2 bytes national). Those fragments are MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT for characters above U+00FF: probe /tmp/adj/probe/cs1.cob - 01 A PIC X(3) VALUE '€é' holds U+20AC in memory (ORD(A(1:1)) = 8365, DISPLAY prints '€é'), FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(A)=3, but the storage image CONVERT(A ANY ANUM HEX) = '3FE920' (€ -> 0x3F via ByteSub), and a sequential file writes it as '?' with no status (PB690, SequentialConnector Latin-1). So the code fixes a behavior (UTF-16 repertoire in memory, Latin-1 one-byte encoding at every byte boundary) and no row states the alphanumeric set's characters or its encoding. Harm: silent. Owning note: PB690 (open, blocked on owner - 'The determination goes in CONFORMANCE.md as DOC-A.1-31/-34 rows'); register umbrella PB160/A11. Referenced, not re-reported.

Rule: A.1 item 32 'Computer's coded character set (coded character values for certain COBOL items). This item is required. This item shall be documented ... If values are determined at runtime, documentation shall specify the manner'. §8.1.2: 'The implementor shall specify one and only one alphanumeric coded character value associated with each of the following COBOL elements' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)) and the national twin. CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-32 |' row; no statement of the coded values of SPACE/QUOTE/ZERO, space fill, the editing characters or the default currency character. Code fixes them (compile-time constants): FillChar maps ZERO->'0' U+0030, SPACE->' ' U+0020, QUOTE->'"' U+0022 in both classes (PB1397 probe: MOVE ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE TO PIC X(3)/N(3) -> '000|000', '[   |   ]', '"""|"""'). Behavior consistent; documentation obligation unmet => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning note: PB1397 (open) - 'Write DOC-A.1-25, -26, -32, -44, -74 and -95 rows'. Referenced, not re-reported.

Rule: A.1 item 34 'Computer's coded character set (for literals, correspondence between compile-time and runtime character sets, when conversion takes place). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon there being a difference between the compile-time and runtime computer's coded character sets. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2: 'The implementor shall define the correspondence of each character of the compile-time coded character set with an associated character in the runtime coded character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). Code: the compile-time computer's coded character set (the set 'used in the memory of the computer during compilation', §8.1.2 first sentence) is the .NET UTF-16 string the source is decoded into by CompilationInputs.ReadAllText; literals are emitted as C# string literals and the runtime alphanumeric/national sets are the same UTF-16 code units, so NO compile-time->runtime conversion exists (probe cs1.cob: VALUE '€é' -> ORD 8365 at run time, i.e. the compile-time character unchanged). The condition the item is conditioned on (a difference between the sets) does not arise; the facility is absent. CONFORMANCE.md states neither the identity nor the absence (no DOC-A.1-34 row), and PB690 (open) already names 'DOC-A.1-31/-34 rows' as owed - though PB690's file-encoding question is really item 31's, not item 34's (item 34 is literals only). Recorded NOT-IMPLEMENTED (facility absent) pending an owner-level posture for conditional items whose condition is unmet (finding conditional-facility-absent-posture). Owning note: PB690 (open).

editions: 2002, 2014, 2023 (UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE with the r2-r4 locale split; the no-locale mapping applies to every edition that has the functions)
notes: Rule: A.1 item 35 'Computer's coded character set (correspondence between lowercase and uppercase letters when a locale is not in effect). This item is required. This item need not be documented' (cite.py --check A.1 'This item need not be documented in the implementor' -> OK §A.1 35)). §15.97.4 r4 'When a locale is not in effect, the implementor defines the correspondence of lowercase letters to uppercase letters' -> OK §15.97.4 4); §15.57.4 r4 twin -> OK §15.57.4 4). No documentation obligation, so (a) is waived; CONFORMANCE.md nevertheless states it voluntarily in §3 (DETERMINATION L9, 'the invariant tables', simple one-code-unit-to-one correspondence, ß stays ß). Code: CobolIntrinsics.UpperCase = s.ToUpperInvariant(), LowerCase = s.ToLowerInvariant() - a defined, length-preserving (r5) correspondence; the locale arms (r2/r3) route through CobolLocale. Probe /tmp/adj/probe/cs1.cob: UPPER-CASE('aéß') -> 'AÉß', LOWER-CASE('ÉA') -> 'éa'. Test: conformance:2002/pb64t5_case_locale_phrase line PLAIN - a program with no classification and no phrase maps 'i' -> 'I' (ORD 74) even while LC_CTYPE is Turkish, i.e. r4's implementor correspondence and not the locale's. Caveat for the refuter: the golden pins the UPPER-CASE direction of r4 only; LOWER-CASE r4 is verified by probe and by code reading, not by a golden. Owning note: none (PB738's 'item 35' is Annex E.3.3, unrelated).

Rule: A.1 item 36 'Computer's coded character set (when composite alphanumeric and national, mapping of characters to each). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for a composite alphanumeric and national computer character set. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2 'When these are implemented as one character set, the implementor shall specify the characters that map into the computer's alphanumeric coded character set and the characters that map into the computer's national coded character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). CONDITION IS MET: CONFORMANCE.md rows DOC-A.1-33 and DOC-A.1-188 state 'Both native repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position' - one coded character set for both classes (§8.1.2 NOTE 2's UTF-16 shape). CONFORMANCE.md has NO '| DOC-A.1-36 |' row stating which characters map into the alphanumeric set. Row 33's 'TOTAL IDENTITY' implies all 65,536 code units are alphanumeric, but the code treats the alphanumeric set as Latin-1 at every byte boundary: probe /tmp/adj/probe/cs1.cob - PIC X holding '€' (ORD 8365 in memory) has storage image 0x3F (ByteSub, EC-DATA-CONVERSION only when checked), and a sequential file writes '?' silently (PB690). So the mapping the item demands is both unwritten and not single-valued in the code. Harm: silent (a user cannot learn which characters an alphanumeric item holds losslessly). Owning note: none names item 36 (grep 'DOC-A.1-36\|item 36' hits only Annex E.3.3 item 36 notes PB434/PB438/PB441/PB595); PB690 (open, blocked on owner) owns the file-encoding half and names rows 31/34. Reported as finding charset-determination-unwritten-and-split with 31/38.

notes: Rule: A.1 item 37 'Computer's coded character set (when more than one encoding, the mechanism for selecting encoding for runtime). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for more than one encoding of a computer's coded character set. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2 'If more than one encoding of the computer's character set is supported, the implementor shall specify the mechanism for selecting the encoding for use at runtime' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 'If more than one encoding of the computer' -> OK §8.1.2 3)). Code: the computer's coded character set in memory is fixed as .NET UTF-16 code units; grep of every Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable in src/Cobol.Net.Runtime (the RuntimeConfig-registered set: CLDR dir, collation cache, switches, locale, key-check, clock pin) finds no encoding selector, and the CLI has no --encoding option. (StandardStreams forcing UTF-8 on the console is device conversion - items 1/56 - not an encoding of the computer's coded character set; CODE-SET is a file's set, §13.18.13.) The facility the item is conditioned on is ABSENT, so the obligation is not incurred, but no posture is recorded; same class as items 30 and 34 (finding conditional-facility-absent-posture). Owning note: none (grep 'item 37' hits only A.2/E.3.3/Table-1 item 37 notes PB370/PB597/PB686).

editions: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §8.3.3.2.3 SR2 UTF-8/mixed permission accompanies the national set, 2002+)
notes: Rule: A.1 item 38 'Computer's coded character set (whether UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters recognized in class alphanumeric; applicable syntax and general rules). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for UTF-8 or mixing alphanumeric and national characters in literals and data items of class alphanumeric. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.3.3.2.3 SR2 'An implementation is neither required to recognize nor prohibited from recognizing UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters in format 1 alphanumeric literals. When permitted, the capability shall be optionally available to the user ...; the implementor shall specify any applicable syntax rules' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 -> OK §8.3.3.2.3 2)); §8.3.3.2.4 GR3 c) '...the implementor shall specify the applicable general rules' -> OK §8.3.3.2.4 3) c). Code: an alphanumeric literal accepts ANY UTF-16 character, unconditionally (no option): probe cs1.cob 01 A PIC X(3) VALUE '€é' compiles clean at the default std and holds U+20AC. Whether that is 'mixed alphanumeric and national' depends on the item-31/36 determination of the alphanumeric repertoire, which is unwritten and split (UTF-16 in memory per rows 33/188; one byte / Latin-1 at the storage image and on files - ByteSub '?' and PB690). If € is a national character in class alphanumeric, the capability is always on, contrary to SR2's 'optionally available to the user', and its rules are undocumented; if it is alphanumeric, the item's condition fails but the byte boundary contradicts it. Either way the code fixes a behavior and CONFORMANCE.md has no '| DOC-A.1-38 |' row => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning note: none names item 38 (PB725's 'item 38' is E.3.3). Clustered into finding charset-determination-unwritten-and-split (31/36/38); PB690 owns the file half.
